neighbours.label: a function word in news about a coup, an invasion or international sanctions ('ousted in a coup', 'intervention in Syria', 'after the country invaded')
fire: The general was toppled in a coup last spring, officials said.
Western leaders condemned the military intervention in Libya.
New sanctions followed after the army invaded its neighbor.
Soldiers overthrew the president in a bloody coup at dawn.
Moscow denied any role in the annexation of Crimea.
The minister was deposed in a palace coup that summer.
Allies imposed sanctions on Russia after the invasion of Georgia.
Rebels seized the capital in a coup backed by the army.
quiet: The principal was hired in a town last spring, officials said.
Local leaders praised the new library in Toledo.
New sidewalks followed after the city repaved its streets.
Voters chose the mayor in a quiet election at noon.
Ohio approved a plan for the repair of bridges.
The minister was married in a garden that summer.
Shops offered discounts on shoes after the end of winter.
Students cleaned the park on a day planned by the school.

short: news of coups, invasions and sanctions
notes: Card: ' the' x5, ' in' x5, ' Russian' x3, ' a' x2, '-called', and sanctions, coups and Ukraine in the examples. Probe: ' a' before 'coup' 0.396; ' in' after 'intervention' 0.181; ' the' after 'sanctions after' 0.139; ' dis' 0.047; everyday frames at most 0.012. Readings are modest and near misses are ordinary domestic news.
